subject: Discovery Recap: Tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <pri@acmeai.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery Recap: Tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please let me know if I missed anything or if you'd like to adjust success criteria.

Summary of pains & goals
- Pain: Current generation outputs are inconsistent across agents — downstream systems need deterministic, schema-conformant JSON to run post-processing pipelines.
- Pain: Long tail of prompts require reliable tool/function calling (calling internal APIs and returning structured results) with predictable latency.
- Goal: Produce deterministic structured output (JSON) for 90%+ of cases and provide safe fallbacks for ambiguous inputs.

Current stack
- Frontend: React app with a transaction pipeline that expects a JSON payload from the LLM to invoke billing, risk checks, and enrichment.
- LLM: In-house fine-tuned model for NLU; experiments with open models for lower cost on bulk enrichment.
- Orchestration: Node services that call LLM and then call internal REST APIs.

Success criteria (what "good" looks like)
- JSON schema conformance: Output must validate against a provided JSON schema with 95% pass rate on our 1k eval set.
- Deterministic formatting: For the same input + context, top-1 output must match canonical JSON formatting 90% of runs (seeded evals).
- Tool calling correctness: Agent should call the correct function endpoint with validated args >= 98% on critical flows (billing, risk).
- Latency SLO: p95 response <= 400ms for the interactive flows.

Notes on structured output and agent workflows we discussed
- We prefer explicit function/tool calling over hidden inline JSON because it makes routing and auditability easier.
- When using structured output, we need: (1) a strict JSON schema for each agent type, (2) a deterministic formatting layer (canonical key ordering, trimmed whitespace), and (3) a validation + repair step before any downstream action.

Next steps
1) I attached a short mutual action plan (MAP-acmeai-20260912.xlsx) with milestones and owners.
2) Jordan will send a concise example JSON schema and a 10-case eval set for you to run locally.
3) Dev and your engineering lead to sync on API auth and routing (we suggested JWT exchange + tracing headers).
4) Schedule a 60-min demo next week: Tue/Wed mornings PST preferred.

Ask: Can you confirm the success criteria above and share a sample of the current expected JSON schema (or one representative endpoint) so Jordan can map Redwood's tool-calling flow to your validators?

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0199

Attachment: MAP-acmeai-20260912.xlsx (mutual action plan, milestone owners)

Subject: Re: Discovery Recap: Tool-calling & structured output (JSON schema)

Hi Marissa / Jordan —

Thanks for the thorough recap — this looks right to me. A few clarifications and notes from our side:

Clarifications
- The canonical JSON we validate against is produced by a microservice called payload-validator; I attached a representative schema for the billing call in the thread (see redwood-discovery-map.pdf for a diagram).
- For deterministic formatting: ordering keys consistently is critical because we compute stable signatures (SHA256) on the serialized payload before sending to downstream services.

Constraints
- We cannot accept automatic repairs that change critical fields (amount, user_id) without manual review. Repairs for cosmetic fields (phone formatting) are fine.
- Our infra team prefers that any function/tool call include a correlation_id header so we can trace requests end-to-end.

Agreement on next steps
- We'll review the MAP and share internal owners by EOD tomorrow.
- Can Jordan send the 10-case eval set and the minimal JSON schema for the three agent types we discussed (billing, enrichment, risk)?
- Dev (our engineer) is available Wed 16 Sep 10:00-11:00 PST for a technical sync.

Thanks — looking forward to the demo.

Best,
Priya Shah
Head of Integrations | Acme AI
pri@acmeai.com
